title: Add `check_row_order` argument
description: * Add `check_row_order` argument to `tbl_check()`, `tbl_grade()`, and `tbl_equal()`. When `check_row_order()` is set to false, `object` and `expected` are arranged so that their row orders match before checking for differences in column values.

title: Rename files to include `tbl_` or `vec_` prefixes
Add `tbl_equal()`
description:
* Add `tbl_equal()`, which returns a `TRUE` or `FALSE` value indicating if two tables are equivalent, using the same process as `tbl_check()`.
* `tbl_check()`, `tbl_grade()`, `tbl_check_column()`, `tbl_grade_column()` and `vec_grade()` gain arguments to set whether they will check the levels of factors.
* `vec_check()` and `vec_grade()` now only check factor levels if both `object` and `expected` are factors. In most cases, this difference would be caught earlier by class checking. Previously, calling `vec_check(x, factor(x), check_class = FALSE)` would signal a problem because one vector has levels and the other does not.

Closes #131.

title: Use generic functions to generate class messages
description:
Messages generated by `tbl_grade_class()` now internally call two generic functions:
* `friendly_class()` is an S3 generic that generates class names for single objects.
  * e.g. `friendly_class(character(1))` returns "a text string (class `character`)".
* `hinted_class_message()` is an R7 generic that generates messages when `object` and `expected` are both a specific class.
  * e.g. if `object` is an ungrouped tibble and `expected` is a grouped tibble, `hinted_class_message()` generates a message that suggests using `group_by()`.

Using generic functions allows `tbl_grade_class()` messages to be expanded by adding methods for new classes in tutorial setup code or external packages.

title: Set `pass_if_equal = FALSE` as default in `grade_this_table()`
description: To avoid costly comparisons through `waldo::compare()`. We've found in practice that this behavior should be opt-in (for tables, at least).

title: Export `problem()` and `problem_message()`
description:
This PR exposes some of the problem-related infrastructure of tblcheck, in particular making it easier for other packages to construct `problem` objects with `problem()` and to extend the `problem_message` generic.

1. We now export `problem()`
2. I renamed `tblcheck_message()` to `problem_message()` and moved it next to the other code related to the problem class.
3. We now export `problem_message()` too
4. I renamed `tblcheck_grade()` to `problem_grade()` since this also better describes the generic.

Now that everything is together I think there's a strong case for the generics to live in gradethis — we even called the problem a `gradethis_problem`. I also think this is the perfect use-case for R7, so I think we should wait until that's available on CRAN and then move the problem generics into gradethis and migrate to R7 at the same time.

title: Don't call non-vectors "vectors"
description:
Remove messages with "vector" from the fallback method in `friendly_class()`.
Now if the method falls back, it will always describe the object as an "object".
All atomic vectors types already have an associated friendly class message, so they will still be correctly described as vectors.

``` r
.result <- 1:2
.solution <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
tbl_grade_class()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your result should be an object with class `lm`, but it is a vector
#>   of integers (class `integer`).
#> >

.result <- 1:2
.solution <- c("1", "2")
tbl_grade_class()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your result should be a vector of text (class `character`), but it is
#>   a vector of integers (class `integer`).
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2022-08-09 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #120.

title: Add `ignore_class` argument and ignore `grouped_df` if `check_groups = FALSE`
description:
- Adds argument `ignore_class` to `class` checks (and passed by `table`, `vector`, and `column` checks), specifying class differences to ignore.
  - Unnamed elements are dropped from the list of classes for the purpose of comparison: e.g. `ignore_class = "glue"` will ignore cases where `.result` is `glue`/`character` and `.solution` is `character`, or vice versa.
  - Named elements are treated as equivalent to their names: e.g. `ignore_class = c("integer" = "numeric")` will ignore cases where `.result` is `integer` and `.solution` is `numeric`, or vice versa.
- Table checking now ignores the `grouped_df` class if `check_groups = FALSE`.
- Classes are now checked with `setequal()` instead of `identical()`, so objects with the same classes in different orders will not trigger a `class` problem.

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(tblcheck)

.result   <- data.frame(a = 1, b = 2)
.solution <- tibble(a = 1, b = 2)

tbl_check_class(ignore_class = c("tbl_df", "tbl"))
# No output

.result   <- 1L
.solution <- 1

vec_check_class(ignore_class = c("integer" = "numeric"))
# No output

.result   <- tibble(a = 1, b = 2)
.solution <- tibble(a = 1, b = 2) %>% group_by(b)

tbl_check(check_groups = FALSE)
# No output
```

<sup>Created on 2022-02-08 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #108.

title: Fix column values problem message
description:
Fixes a bug that caused the "I didn't expect your result" message to overwrite the "I didn't expect your ___ column" messages for values problems.


``` r
pkgload::load_all()
#> ℹ Loading tblcheck

.result <- tibble::tibble(x = c(1:5, runif(5)))
.solution <- tibble::tibble(x = c(1:5, runif(5)))
```

## Before

``` r
tbl_grade_column("x")
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   I didn't expect your result to include the values `0.2423`, `0.1420`,
#>   and `0.0605`.
#> >
```

```r
tbl_check_column("x")
#> <tblcheck problem>
#> I didn't expect your result to include the values `0.2423`, `0.1420`, and `0.0605`.
#> $ type    : chr "values"
#> $ expected: num [1:10] 1 2 3 4 5 ...
#> $ actual  : num [1:10] 1 2 3 4 5 ...
#> $ location: chr "column"
#> $ column  : chr "x"
```

## After

```r
tbl_grade_column("x")
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   I didn't expect your `x` column to include the values `0.2423`,
#>   `0.1420`, and `0.0605`.
#> >
```

```r
tbl_check_column("x")
#> <tblcheck problem>
#> I didn't expect your `x` column to include the values `0.2423`, `0.1420`, and `0.0605`.
#> $ type    : chr "values"
#> $ expected: num [1:10] 1 2 3 4 5 ...
#> $ actual  : num [1:10] 1 2 3 4 5 ...
#> $ location: chr "column"
#> $ column  : chr "x"
```

title: Add `tidyselect` support to `tbl_grade()`/`tbl_check()`
description:
Adds argument `cols` to `tbl_grade()` and `tbl_check()` which uses `tidyselect` to specify a subset of columns to grade.

Other columns are ignored, allowing for extraneous columns to be ignored.

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(tblcheck)

random_values <- tibble(x = rnorm(10))

.solution <- random_values %>%
  mutate(z_score = (x - mean(x)) / sd(x))

.result <- random_values %>%
  mutate(
    mean = mean(x),
    sd = sd(x),
    z_score = (x - mean) / sd
  )

tbl_grade()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your table should not have columns named `mean` or `sd`.
#> >

tbl_grade(cols = any_of(names(.solution))) # No output
```

<sup>Created on 2021-10-29 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #83.

title: Add `grade_this_*()` tblcheck grading functions
description:
This PR adds one-stop table and vector grading via three new functions: `grade_this_table()`, `grade_this_column()` and `grade_this_vector()`. They're intended to be used in the same way as `grade_this_code()`, but with a few additions. ``` r library(gradethis) library(tblcheck) library(tibble) ``` Here's a simple demo using a table exercise with a small mistake. ``` r ex <- mock_this_exercise( .solution_code = tibble(x = 1:3, y = letters[x]), .user_code = tibble(x = 1:3, y = c("A", "b", "c")) ) ex_correct <- rlang::env_clone(ex) ex_correct$.result <- ex$.solution ```
User Solution
Code 
tibble(x = 1:3, y = c("A", "b", "c"))
 
tibble(x = 1:3, y = letters[x])
Result 
# A tibble: 3 × 2
      x y    
  <int> <chr>
1     1 A    
2     2 b    
3     3 c    
# A tibble: 3 × 2
      x y    
  <int> <chr>
1     1 a    
2     2 b    
3     3 c
## Grading Tables ``` r # ```{r example-check} grade_this_table()(ex) # ``` #> The first 3 values of your `y` column should be `a`, `b`, and `c`. #> > ``` ``` r # ```{r example-check} grade_this_table(hint = TRUE)(ex) # ``` #> The first 3 values of your `y` column should be `a`, `b`, and `c`. In #> `tibble(x = 1:3, y = c("A", "b", "c"))`, I expected you to call `y = #> [` where you called `y = c()`. #> > ``` ``` r # ```{r example-check} grade_this_table("Great work! You should be proud.")(ex_correct) # ``` #> ``` Roughly equivalent to… ``` r # ```{r example-check} gradethis::grade_this({ gradethis::pass_if_equal() tbl_grade() gradethis::fail() })(ex) # ``` #> The first 3 values of your `y` column should be `a`, `b`, and `c`. #> > ``` ## Grading Columns in Tables ``` r # ```{r example-check} grade_this_column("y")(ex) # ``` #> The first 3 values of your `y` column should be `a`, `b`, and `c`. #> > ``` ## Grading Vectors Here we use `pre_check` to modify `.result` and `.solution`, but if the exercise involved vectors we wouldn’t need to. ``` r # ```{r example-check} grade_this_vector( pre_check = { .result <- .result$y .solution <- .solution$y } )(ex) # ``` #> The first 3 values of your result should be `a`, `b`, and `c`. #> > ```

title: Remove concept of "inconsequential" class differences
description:
`class` checking now finds all differences in classes. This remove previous behavior that would ignore a small set of "inconsequential" differences:

- `integer` vs. `numeric`
- `character` vs. `glue`
- `POSIXct` vs. `POSIXlt`

Surfacing all class differences increases compatibility with other `tblcheck` and `gradethis` functions, like `vec_grade_values()` and `pass_if_equal()`, which may fail because of class differences that `vec_check_class()` previously deemed inconsequential.

This change will require exercise authors to take care in instances where a student may plausibly provide an answer with either of two classes. However, this tradeoff is worthwhile, because these problems were still likely to surface in less identifiable places (e.g. `vec_check_values()` or `pass_if_equal()`).

Closes #71.

title: Make message more informative
description:
- `length` problem message now includes the first missing or unexpected value if two conditions are met:
  - The difference between the expected and actual length ≤ 2.
  - There are ≤ 2 different values between the expected and actual vector.
  - In cases where the vector lengths differ by more than two or where there are more than two different values between the vectors, existing behavior is retained (i.e. only the difference in length is signalled).

``` r
library(tblcheck)

# Lengths differ <= 2 and <= 2 value differences
.result <- 1:3
.solution <- 1:5
vec_grade_length()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your result should contain 5 values, but it has 3 values. I expected
#>   your result to include the value `4`.
#> >

# Lengths differ > 2
.result <- 1:3
.solution <- 1:6
vec_grade_length()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your result should contain 6 values, but it has 3 values.
#> >

# > 2 value differences
.result <- 1:3
.solution <- 4:7
vec_grade_length()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your result should contain 4 values, but it has 3 values.
#> >
```

- `values` problem messages now inform the user of problems after the first `max_diffs` values:

``` r
library(tblcheck)

# Difference within first three values
.result <- 4:13
.solution <- 1:10
vec_grade_values()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   The first 3 values of your result should be `1`, `2`, and `3`, not
#>   `4`, `5`, and `6`.
#> >

# Unexpected values after first three
.result <- c(1:3, 7:13)
.solution <- 1:10
vec_grade_values()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   I didn't expect your result to include the values `11`, `12`, and
#>   `13`.
#> >

# Missing values after first three
.result <- c(1:3, rep(4L, 7))
.solution <- 1:10
vec_grade_values()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   I expected your result to include the values `5`, `6`, and `7`.
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2021-10-21 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

<sup>Created on 2021-10-13 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

- Include `vec_*_length()` as alias for `vec_*_dimensions()`

For #65.

title: Check names order
description:
This PR adds a check in `tbl_check_names()` to determine if the names are in the correct order.

``` r
.result <- 1:10
names(.result) <- letters[1:10]
.solution <- 1:10
names(.solution) <- letters[10:1]
vec_grade_names()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your result's names were not in the expected order. The first 3 names
#>   of your result should be `j`, `i`, and `h`.
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2021-09-17 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

By default, the order of names is not checked for tables, but this can be performed by setting `check_order` to `TRUE`.

``` r
.result   <- starwars %>% mutate(inches = height / 2.54, pounds = mass * 2.205)
.solution <- starwars %>% mutate(pounds = mass * 2.205, inches = height / 2.54)
tbl_grade_table()
# No output

.result   <- starwars %>% relocate(species, .before = 1)
.solution <- starwars %>% relocate(species, .after = 1)
tbl_grade_table(check_order = TRUE)
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your table's columns were not in the expected order. The first 3
#>   columns of your table should be `name`, `species`, and `height`.
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2021-09-17 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #56.

title: Standardize problem types
description:
Standardize problem types as described in #51.

- Problems now all take the form `[specfic-check](_[optional-prefix])`.
  - e.g. `levels_reversed`, `values_order` or `dimensions_n`
- Prefixes for general checking functions are removed in favor of adding classes based on the general function (`table_problem`, `column_problem`, or `vector_problem`).
  - `problem`s gain a `location` element which stores this information, akin to `type` for specific function information.
- Each type of problem now has a single `tbl_message()` method, which determines whether to generate table, column, or vector versions of its messages using `if_problem()`.
- `_diffs` problems are removed. `tbl_message.values()` and `tbl_message.levels()` now handle cases where specific differences both can and cannot be displayed.
  - As a result, `max_diffs` no longer needs to be passed to any `check` functions. `tbl_message()` exclusively handles `max_diffs`.

Closes #51 and #53.

description: Set Alex as new maintainer and update package title and description

title: Separate problem generation out of general checking functions
description:
Adds `tbl_*_missing()`, which checks for missing columns, and `vec_check_values()`, which checks for mismatched values between vectors.

This change means that the general checking functions `tbl_check_column()` and `vec_check_vector()` no longer generate problems – all problem generation is handled by calling specific functions.

Closes #52.

title: Check for reversed levels and report both `actual` and `expected` levels
description:
Add message for the special case where levels are reversed from expected.

``` r
.result <- starwars %>% 
  mutate(species = fct_reorder(species, height, median, .desc = TRUE))
.solution <- starwars %>% 
  mutate(species = fct_reorder(species, height, median, .desc = FALSE))
tbl_grade_table()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#> Your `species` column's levels were not in the expected
#>   order. The order of the levels should be reversed.
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2021-09-08 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Also report both `actual` and `expected` levels when level orders differ without being reversed. Previously only `expected` levels were reported, which made it hard to diagnose problems in tables where level order is not readily visible.

``` r
.result   <- starwars %>% mutate(species = fct_inorder(species))
.solution <- starwars %>% mutate(species = fct_shuffle(species))
tbl_grade_table()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your `species` column's levels were not in the expected order. The
#>   first 3 levels of your `species` column should be `Pau'an`,
#>   `Wookiee`, and `Hutt`, but they were `Human`, `Droid`, and `Wookiee`.
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2021-09-08 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Closes #46 and #47.

title: Add `vec_` aliases for class and names checks
description:
Adds `vec_check_class()` & `vec_grade_class()` and `vec_check_names()` & `vec_grade_names()` as aliases for the respective `tbl_` functions.

These functions work equally well for data frames or vectors, so the underlying code is not changed. This simply makes it easier for authors writing exercises with vectors to discover these functions.

Closes #39.

title: Evaluate `tbl_grade()` in `gradethis` env
description:
Passes `env` into `tbl_grade()` so that `tbl_grade_*()` functions will follow the same options as `gradethis` functions.

```r
ex <- mock_this_exercise(
  .user_code     = "select(starwars, mass)",
  .solution_code = "select(starwars, height)",
  setup_global   = "library(dplyr)"
)

gradethis_setup(fail.hint = TRUE)

grade_this({
  tbl_grade_names()
})(ex)
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your table should have a column named `height`. Your
#>   table should not have a column named `mass`. In
#>   `select(starwars, mass)`, I expected `height` where you
#>   wrote `mass`.
#> >
```

Closes #38.

title: Use `vec_` prefix for vector and level checking
description:
- Renames functions to `vec_grade_vector()`, `vec_check_vector()`, `vec_grade_levels()` and `vec_check_levels()`.
- Adds `vec_*_length()`, which provides a streamlined version of `tbl_*_dimensions()` for 1-dimensional vectors. `tbl_check_dimensions()` includes a call to `vec_check_length()` internally.
- Allows function to begin with `tbl_` or `vec_` when testing with `tblcheck_test_grade()`.

Closes #36.

title: Check if character vectors have the same number of characters
description:
Adds `tbl_check_nchar()` and `tbl_grade_nchar()`, which check to see if all elements of a character vector have the same number of characters. If they do, check if that is the same as the expected number of characters.

``` r
.result <- strrep(letters, 1:26)
.solution <- strrep(letters, 2)
tbl_check_nchar()
#> <tblcheck problem>
#> Every element of your result should be 2 characters long, but it does not have a consistent character length.
#> $ type    : chr "inconsistent_nchar"
#> $ expected: int 2

.result <- letters
.solution <- strrep(letters, 2)
tbl_check_nchar()
#> <tblcheck problem>
#> Every element of your result should be 2 characters long, but it is all 1 character long.
#> $ type    : chr "nchar"
#> $ expected: int 2
#> $ actual  : int 1
```

`tbl_*_nchar()` is only intended for checking character vectors. If `object` and `expected` are not both character vectors, they are dispatched to `tbl_check_class()`.

``` r
.result <- 1:26
.solution <- strrep(letters, 2)
tbl_check_nchar()
#> <tblcheck problem>
#> Your result should be a vector of text (class `character`), but it is a vector of integers (class `integer`).
#> $ type           : chr "class"
#> $ expected       : chr "character"
#> $ actual         : chr "integer"
#> $ expected_length: int 26
#> $ actual_length  : int 26
```

 If `expected` does not have a consistent number of characters, a warning is produced and no grade is applied.

``` r
.result <- letters
.solution <- strrep(letters, 1:26)
tbl_check_nchar()
#> Warning in tbl_check_nchar(): `expected` does not have a consistent number of
#> characters.
#> NULL
```

<sup>Created on 2021-08-26 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1.9000)</sup>


This check could be helpful in exercises like:
- https://github.com/rstudio/academyLifeSciences/issues/64
- https://github.com/rstudio/academyLifeSciences/pull/22

title: Check levels
description:
Add `tbl_check_levels()` and `tbl_grade_levels()` to test for differences between the levels of two factors.

`tbl_check_levels()` can return two new problem classes: `n_levels_problem` if the number of levels is different than expected, and `levels_problem` if the level labels are different. These problem classes can be prefixed with `vector_` or `column_` if called through `tbl_*_vector()` or `tbl_*_column()`.

``` r
.result   <- as.factor(c("a", "b", "b"))
.solution <- as.factor(c("a", "b", "c"))
tbl_grade_levels()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your result should have 3 levels, but it has 2 levels.
#> >
.result   <- as.factor(c("a", "b", "c"))
.solution <- as.factor(c("x", "y", "z"))
tbl_grade_levels()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your result should have the levels `x`, `y`, and `z`. Your result
#>   should not have the levels `a`, `b`, or `c`.
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2021-08-23 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

- [x] Add `tbl_check_levels()` and `tbl_grade_levels()`
- [x] Check number of levels
- [x] Check level labels
- [x] Check level order
- [x] Add `tbl_message()` methods for levels problems
- [x] Call `tbl_check_levels()` in `tbl_check_vector()`
- [x] Add tests

Depends on #25.
Closes #32.

title: Make `tblcheck` messages translatable
description:
This PR refactors `tbl_message()` functions so that their messages can be translated using `gettext()`.

``` r
tbl_grade_vector(1:10, letters[1:10])
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your result should be a vector of text (class `character`), but it is
#>   a vector of integers (class `integer`).
#> >
Sys.setenv("LANGUAGE" = "es")
tbl_grade_vector(1:10, letters[1:10])
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Su resultado debe ser un vector de texto (clase `character`), pero es
#>   un vector de números enteros (clase `integer`).
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2021-08-17 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

New translations can be added in the `po` directory and built using `tools::update_pkg_po(".")`. 

Relies on #25.
Closes #19.

Todo:

- [ ] Support translation of `combine_words()`

title: Add examples for all `tblcheck` functions
description:
This PR adds examples for all `tblcheck` functions.
Closes #20.

title: Check groups in `tblcheck`
description:
This PR adds `tbl_check_groups()` and `tbl_grade_groups()`, which check that tables have the same groups set by `dplyr::group_by()`. These functions can be called on their own and are also by default called within `tbl_check_table()` and `tbl_grade_table()`. This can be disabled with the argument `check_groups = FALSE`.

``` r
.result   <- tibble(a = letters, b = a) %>% group_by(a)
.solution <- tibble(a = letters, b = a) %>% group_by(b)
tbl_grade_table()
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect]
#>   Your table should be grouped by `b`. Your table should not be grouped
#>   by `a`.
#> >
```

<sup>Created on 2021-08-16 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

This PR is built on top of #25, so should be merged after that.

title: Modernize `tblcheck` vignette
description:
This PR updates the vignette to give examples in the form of `learnr` chunks rather than internal R code.
It also uses examples derived from realistic lessons rather than contrived examples.

title: Implement `tblcheck` problem messages with S3
description:
This PR implements an S3 system for generating messages from `problem`s.

`problem`s now have classes specifying the type of problem, e.g. 
``` r
.result   <- c(a = 1, b = 2, c = 3)
.solution <- c(x = 1, y = 2, z = 3)
class(tbl_check_names())
#> [1] "names_problem"     "tblcheck_problem"  "gradethis_problem"
#> [4] "list"
```
<sup>Created on 2021-08-13 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

When `tbl_check_*()` functions are called within other functions, additional classes are appended:
``` r
.result   <- tibble(a = 1:3)
.solution <- tibble(a = 4:6)
class(tbl_check_table())
#> [1] "column_values_problem" "vector_values_problem" "values_problem"       
#> [4] "tblcheck_problem"      "gradethis_problem"     "list"
```
<sup>Created on 2021-08-13 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

The existing `tbl_message_*()` family of functions is replaced with a single generic `tbl_message()` and methods for each relevant `problem` class. This reduces the internal complexity of `tbl_message()` methods, because methods no longer need to determine whether they should generate messages for a table, column, or vector – this is determined by the problem class.

`tbl_grade()` is also significantly simplified, as it no longer needs to determine which `tbl_message_*()` function to call – this is now handled by S3 dispatch.

Closes #22, #23, #24, and #34.

title: Split functions into `tbl_grade_*()` and `tbl_check_*()`
Update `check_names()`
description: Update `check_names()` to use `unit` and `prefix` like other `check_` functions and add option to use `check_names()` within `check_vector()` (enabled by default)

title: Check table class
description:
Check that the table has the expected class(es) in `check_table()` (e.g. check that the submitted table is a tibble rather than a data frame). Closes #13.

Adds a function `check_class()` to compare the classes of two objects. This function is now used internally in both `check_table()` and `check_column()`.

title: Return early from grading functions
description:
Fixes #9

Currently, the `check_*()` functions only exhibit "early return" behavior when called in a gradethis context, i.e. inside `grade_this()`. This means that without calling handlers, or `tryCatch()`, to handle or catch the `gradethis_graded` condition, the `check_*()` functions execute in their entirety without returning early. Since we generally expect the `check_*()` functions to return the first grade and stop looking further, I've added `return_fail()` and `return_if_graded()` to achieve this behavior.

- `return_fail()` returns from the calling function with the `fail()` grade
- `return_if_graded()` can be wrapped around an expression that _may_ produce a grade, and if it does, it will trigger an early return from the caller function with the grade.

In both case, the early return behavior can be turned off by setting `options(tblcheck.return_first_grade = FALSE)`.

Additionally, I added `tblcheck_test_grade()` which takes an expression ending in a call to one of the `check_*()` functions and executes the check in all three environments: first without any calling handlers, then with calling handlers on `gradethis_graded`, and finally within a mock exercise in `gradethis::grade_this()`.

I updated all of the tests to use `tblcheck_test_grade()`, which returns a single grade after testing that all three methods produce the same grade. This pairs nicely with `expect_grade()`, the new helper function for testing a `gradethis_graded` object.

title: Make `check_names()` use `.result` and `.solution` by default
description: Unlike other `check_` functions, `check_names()` does not currently have default arguments for `object` and `expected`. This sets  `.result` and `.solution` as defaults so `check_names()` works the same as the other functions.

title: Add `check_vector()`
description: Add `check_vector()` function to compare a vector to an expected result outside of a table and update `check_column()` to use `check_vector()` internally. Resolves #7.

title: `check_table()` returns a final grade with with a default of `pass()`
description:
A proposed solution for #5. I've added a new argument, `final_grade`, to `check_table()` where the default is `pass()` that is returned as the final grade if all checks pass.

```r
library(gradethis)
library(tblcheck)

ex <- gradethis::mock_this_exercise(
  .user_code = tibble::tibble(a = letters[1:3], b = a, c = a),
  .solution_code = tibble::tibble(a = letters[1:3], b = a, c = a)
)

grader <- gradethis::grade_this(
  tblcheck::check_table()
) 

grader(ex)
#> <gradethis_graded: [Correct] Magnificent! Correct!>
```

Or you can give your own final grade

```r
ex <- gradethis::mock_this_exercise(
  .user_code = tibble::tibble(a = letters[1:3], b = a, c = a),
  .solution_code = tibble::tibble(a = letters[1:3], b = a, c = a)
)

grader <- gradethis::grade_this(
  tblcheck::check_table(
    final_grade = pass("Great work! Your table had {nrow(.result)} rows in it!")
  )
) 

grader(ex)
#> <gradethis_graded: [Correct] Great work! Your table had 3 rows in it!>
```

Or no final grade by setting `final = NULL`

```r
ex <- gradethis::mock_this_exercise(
  .user_code = tibble::tibble(a = letters[1:3], b = a, c = a),
  .solution_code = tibble::tibble(a = letters[1:3], b = a, c = a)
)

grader <- gradethis::grade_this(
  tblcheck::check_table(final_grade = NULL)
) 

grader(ex)
# invisible NULL
```

title: Refactor tests
description:
I refactored the tests to avoid going all the way to `learnr` to test that `check_table()` and `check_column()` work as expected. Instead, we make sure they work within the `gradethis` context and rely on the tests in `gradethis` to ensure that the integration with learnr will be handled correctly.

I also moved the helper expectations into an R script inside the package, based on [the advice in testthat](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/test_dir.html#special-files).

title: docs: fix typos in roxygen documentation
description:
## Summary

Fixes 8 typos in roxygen documentation. Edits are made in the roxygen comments under `R/`, and the corresponding `man/*.Rd` files are updated to match so the tree stays consistent without needing a `devtools::document()` round-trip. Documentation only - no exported function, argument or object name is changed.

- **R/tbl_check_names.R**, **R/tbl_check_groups.R**, **R/tbl_check_dimensions.R**: `the names/groups/dimensions of two object are the same` -> `... of two objects are the same` (all three titles share the wording, so all three are corrected)
- **R/tbl_check_names.R**: `` `tbl_check_names()` and `vec_check_names()` returns a list `` -> `... return a list` (compound subject)
- **R/tbl_check_names.R**: `` `tbl_grade_names()` and `vec_grade_names()` returns a failing grade `` -> `... return a failing grade`
- **R/vec_check_values.R**: `Checks that two vectors are contain the same values` -> `Checks that two vectors contain the same values`
- **R/tbl_check_column.R**: `` `object` doesn't contain a column named column. `` -> ``` `object` doesn't contain a column named `column`. ``` (every other bullet in that `@section Problems` block already code-formats `column`)
- **R/tbl_check_column.R**: `` @param check_levels ... Whether to check that `column` and has the same [factor levels][levels()] `` -> `` ... Whether to check that `column` has the same [factor levels][levels()] `` (stray `and`; the sibling `check_class`, `check_length`, `check_values` and `check_names` params all read `Whether to check that `column` has the same ...`)

Regenerated `man/` files touched: `tbl_check_names.Rd`, `tbl_check_groups.Rd`, `tbl_check_dimensions.Rd`, `vec_check_values.Rd`, `tbl_check_column.Rd`.

Note on the singular `returns`: the other `- `fn()` returns ...` bullets across the package have a single function as the subject and are correct as written, so they are deliberately left alone. Only the two lines in `tbl_check_names.R` have two functions joined by `and`.
